solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rye beer vessel amongst empty kegs

indicators.note: amongst places one thing inside the surrounding letters of another
an empty word has had its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

blocks.note: the outside letters of kegs
vas is the anatomical term for a vessel or duct

explanation.surface: A brewer's note on where the rye beer is stored, among some drained barrels.
explanation.walkthrough: VAS sits inside K...S. Kvass is a Russian fermented drink made from rye bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Kvass is a mildly alcoholic Slavic drink brewed from rye bread, so it is literally a rye beer.

clue.text: Complex tone exuding Canadian singer’s depth?

indicators.note: exuding means giving something off, so a letter leaks out of the singer's name

blocks.note: k.d. lang is the Canadian singer-songwriter
d is the standard abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A music critic wonders whether a Canadian singer's rich timbre is losing its depth.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the D from KDLANG. Klang is the German-derived term, found in Chambers, for a tone made up of a fundamental plus its overtones.
explanation.definitionFit: A klang is a musical sound comprising a fundamental and its harmonics, hence a compound or complex tone.

clue.text: Red can counter the law lying about everything

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the word for can is read backwards
about here means turned round, so the word for everything is read the other way

blocks.note: can and lav are both slang for a toilet
the law is everyday slang for the police
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone accuses the police of lying about everything, while a can of something red sits nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: Lying simply places one piece beside the next. Can is American slang for a lavatory, and lav is the British short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Valpolicella is a well-known Italian wine from near Verona, and it is almost always red.

clue.text: High fashion evolves a lot, madam spending millions

indicators.note: something that evolves changes its form, so these letters develop into a new order
spending means giving up, so the letter for millions is paid out of the fodder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A fashion writer observes that haute couture changes a great deal, with a wealthy madam spending millions on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one M from A LOT MADAM, then rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alta moda is the Italian phrase for haute couture, the exclusive top end of the clothing trade.

clue.text: North stopping to decide, South’s returned spades

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the letter for north fills a space inside the next word
returned means sent back, so the whole assembled string is read in reverse

blocks.note: to seal a deal is to settle or decide it
N is the abbreviation for north
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A bridge commentary: North interrupts to make a call and South plays back a spade.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes into SEAL to make SENAL, S is added, and the lot is reversed. A slane is a turf-cutting spade used in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanes are narrow spades for cutting peat or turf, so plural spades describes them as a general category.

clue.text: Into past acting in readiness for Shakespeare

indicators.note: acting suggests the letters are performing a different role, taking up a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor slipping into the past, getting ready to perform Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase occurs in Shakespeare, who uses it of soldiers fully armed and prepared; for Shakespeare marks it as his usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's phrase means fully equipped and prepared in every particular, the archaic sense of being ready.

clue.text: One in shop put back head-ornament

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the verb that follows
put back means returned the other way, so the combined string runs backwards

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to shop someone is to inform on them, to rat on them

explanation.surface: Someone in a shop puts a headpiece back on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: I inside RAT gives RAIT, which reversed is the answer. Shop is British slang for betraying someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiar is a poetic short form of tiara, a jewelled band or crown worn on the head.

clue.text: Excellent entertainment, core ingredient of jamborees?

indicators.note: the core of a word is its very centre, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: a boff is a hit show or a big laugh, a piece of successful entertainment
the fifth of nine letters

explanation.surface: A reviewer praising the fun that lies at the heart of scout jamborees.
explanation.walkthrough: Boff is American showbusiness slang for a hit or a belly laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffo is American slang for very successful or terrific, a box-office term of high praise.

clue.text: Sudden precipitation perhaps uniting Britain’s left?

indicators.note: left here means departed, so the abbreviation for Britain has gone from the word

blocks.note: bonding means joining together
B is an abbreviation for Britain, as on car plates

explanation.surface: A political commentary on whether a sudden event might unite the British left.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's left reads as Britain having left, a Brexit nod: B leaves BONDING. Onding is Scots for a heavy fall of rain or snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An onding is a Scottish word for an onset or downpour, a heavy burst of rain or snow.

clue.text: Irish assembly that is accepted by Sinn Fein recalled

indicators.note: being accepted by something means being taken inside it
recalled means called back, so the abbreviation runs backwards

blocks.note: SF is the usual abbreviation of Sinn Fein, the Irish republican party
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A report that an Irish gathering has been approved by the party, then the decision withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinn Fein is the Irish republican party; its two-letter abbreviation is the one that gets turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A feis is a traditional Irish festival or gathering, especially of music and dance, hence an assembly.

clue.text: Limestone table’s right for me unusually

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters appear in an uncommon arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, with the s
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: A homeowner says the stone top of a table suits them unusually well.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is TABLES, R and FOR ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Forest Marble is a shelly Jurassic limestone from Wychwood Forest in Oxfordshire, used for building and paving.

clue.text: What makes pets walk ahead?

blocks.note: read as an instruction whose result is the word pets: an anagram signal followed by its fodder

explanation.surface: A puzzled owner asks what gets the pets to stride on in front.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer reads as an instruction, out signalling a rearrangement of STEP, and following it produces PETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstep is to step beyond or outpace someone, which amounts to walking on ahead of them.

clue.text: Bumbling a lot in all childish speech?

indicators.note: bumbling means muddled and clumsy, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A toddler bumbling about, babbling a great deal in baby talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: lallation is babbling, or saying L for R as small children do.
explanation.definitionFit: Lallation is infantile babbling, or the substitution of L sounds for R, both typical of young children.

clue.text: Arsenal’s wingers set upon sacrificial block

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so only the two end letters are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of Arsenal
tar is a Shakespearean verb meaning to incite or set on, as with dogs

explanation.surface: A football story: Arsenal's wide players are attacked, as if sacrificed on the chopping block.
explanation.walkthrough: Wingers looks like football players but only takes the outer letters of Arsenal, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the raised table or stone on which sacrifices were offered in ancient worship.

clue.text: Source of riches I’d try moving after settlement

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters change places

blocks.note: a pa is a fortified Maori village or settlement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prospector says that once they have settled, they will move on to try their luck at striking it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the rearranged letters behind PA, a New Zealand word for a Maori settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay dirt is ground rich enough in gold to make mining worthwhile, and idiomatically any profitable discovery.

clue.text: Country girl sources folk dances

blocks.note: mor is a dialect word for a girl; country signals the regional usage
the rise of a river is its source

explanation.surface: A country girl provides material for traditional English dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Country looks like a nation but marks a rustic dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris is a traditional English dance by costumed performers with bells and sticks; morrises are such performances.

clue.text: Bampots bet on rustic game

blocks.note: to go a sum is to stake or wager it
places the first piece before the second
merils, or merels, is the old board game also called nine men's morris

explanation.surface: Fools gamble on some old country pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: Bampot is Scottish slang for an idiot, and gomeril is the Scots word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are Scots words for a foolish or stupid person, so gomerils and bampots are synonyms.

clue.text: Nothing stopping ex-con back in parish to become darker member of flock?

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the letter for nothing fills a gap inside the next word
the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: O looks like zero, nothing
an old lag is a former prisoner
last letter of parish
to tan is to become darker

explanation.surface: A reformed ex-convict returns to the parish and becomes a dark sheep of the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: Member of flock looks like a churchgoer; it is a sheep. The loaghtan is a brown-fleeced breed native to the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx loaghtan is a breed of sheep, so one is literally an animal belonging to a flock.

clue.text: Acoustic device picking up lines by Catholic head of state

indicators.note: picking up means taking on board, so the lines go inside the device

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Catholic
audio equipment handles sound
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled

explanation.surface: A sound system picks up remarks made by a Catholic leader.
explanation.walkthrough: By puts the Catholic abbreviation alongside, here in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Caudillo is the Spanish title for a military leader or dictator, used most famously by Franco as head of state.

clue.text: Heavy blow stokes Scottish lord

blocks.note: S is a physics symbol for the stokes, a unit of viscosity
losh is a Scots minced form of Lord, used as an exclamation

explanation.surface: A violent blow fires up a Scottish nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Stokes looks like a verb but is the unit of viscosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A slosh is a slang word for a heavy punch or wallop, as in to slosh someone.

clue.text: No date on buyer’s option in report one’s happy in saying

indicators.note: in puts the preceding abbreviations inside the word for report

blocks.note: to say is to report
n.d. is the bibliographic abbreviation for no date
b.o. is the commercial abbreviation for buyer's option

explanation.surface: A trader reports that an undated buyer's option means someone will be happy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the saying happy as a sandboy, describing someone who is perfectly content.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial sandboy appears in the phrase happy as a sandboy, so he is the figure whose contentment the expression celebrates.

clue.text: Suggestion of estate, go and tax ploughed area of land

indicators.note: a mere suggestion of a word is just a hint of it, its opening letter
ploughed earth is turned over and churned, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: first letter of estate
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A landowner muses that a hint of estate tax will go on a ploughed field.
explanation.walkthrough: The six letters E, GO and TAX are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxgate, or oxgang, was the old measure of land an ox could plough in a season, about fifteen acres.

clue.text: What initiates attributes? Chromosome’s helping

indicators.note: what initiates a word is whatever starts it, its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of attributes
idant was Weismann's term for a chromosome

explanation.surface: A geneticist asks what triggers inherited traits, crediting the chromosome's help.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in Chromosome's is read as is, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aidant is an old word, from French, for giving aid; it means assisting or supportive.

clue.text: I for one uttered frank confession

indicators.note: uttered means spoken out loud, so the phrase is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: I is one example of a vowel

explanation.surface: Someone owns up and makes a candid admission in their own words.
explanation.walkthrough: I for one looks like a speaker volunteering; it means the letter I is an example of a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open declaration or admission, so it is a candid acknowledgement of something.

clue.text: Charlie to share a room with Penny

blocks.note: to chum with someone is to share lodgings with them
joins the two pieces
p is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: Two people, Charlie and Penny, agree to room together.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie looks like a name or the NATO letter C; it is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both charlie and chump are British slang for a silly or foolish person.

clue.text: I keep stocking hard willow

blocks.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
an osier is a willow used for basketwork

explanation.surface: A gardener says they keep a stock of tough willow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the first person: the answer is someone who keeps stockings in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosier sells socks and stockings, so in shop terms such a trader keeps hosiery in stock.

clue.text: A fizzy drink’s packing energy virtually

indicators.note: packing means stuffing something inside, so the word for energy goes within the drink

blocks.note: taken as written
soda is a fizzy drink, with the s
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A soft drink is said to be practically bursting with energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of drink's is part of the wordplay, giving a plural rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: As good as is an idiom meaning practically or all but, the same as virtually.

clue.text: Openings for sleeves, correct indeed!

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so each word gives up its start

blocks.note: first letter of sleeves
first letter of correct
yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A tailor confirms the armholes are right.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the starts of sleeves and correct plus a word for indeed spell out what the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A scye is the armhole of a garment, the opening into which a sleeve is sewn.

clue.text: Returning couch that hurts back to furniture outlet

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for couch is read backwards
the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a bed is a couch to sleep on
ouch is what you say when something hurts
last letter of furniture

explanation.surface: A shopper takes back an uncomfortable sofa to the furniture store.
explanation.walkthrough: Furniture outlet looks like a shop; the definition is outlet alone. A debouche is an opening or exit, from French.
explanation.definitionFit: A debouche is an opening or way out, especially where a river or troops emerge, so an outlet.

clue.text: Malaysian wanting a short jacket

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the following letter is missing from the word

blocks.note: the Bajau are a people of Sabah in Malaysia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Malaysian person needs a short coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A from BAJAU. Wanting looks like desiring but means missing.
explanation.definitionFit: The baju is a short loose jacket or tunic worn in Malaysia and Indonesia.

clue.text: Cross about part of sauce spilling over?

indicators.note: spilling means letting something fall out, so a letter drops from the word

blocks.note: c is short for circa, about
a roux is the flour-and-butter base of many sauces
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A cook is annoyed at sauce boiling over the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from ROUX and put C in front. Cross looks like angry; it is the Latin-derived noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Crux is the Latin word for a cross, still used in English for that sense in heraldry and astronomy.

clue.text: Squashed by newspaper, sad end for poor bluebottle

indicators.note: something squashed by another is pressed inside it
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: blat is slang for a newspaper
wo is an archaic spelling of woe, sorrow
last letter of poor

explanation.surface: A fly is swatted flat with a rolled-up paper, a sad end for the poor thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bluebottle looks like the fly; it is the cornflower, which also goes by that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Blawort is an old Scottish name for the cornflower, which is also called the bluebottle for its blue flowers.

clue.text: Marsupial in reserve with short beak

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a bird's bill is its beak
something put by is kept in reserve

explanation.surface: A wildlife reserve houses a marsupial with a stubby snout.
explanation.walkthrough: The beak piece comes first although the clue gives it last.
explanation.definitionFit: The bilby is an Australian bandicoot with long ears, a pouched mammal and so a marsupial.

clue.text: Possibly bitter about dispute — not right output from RI?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for bitter wraps around the rest
not right means the abbreviation for right is taken out

blocks.note: bitter is a kind of beer, so possibly an ale
a quarrel is a dispute
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pub argument, possibly over bitter, from which the right side withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: The RI is the Royal Institute of Painters in Water Colours, hence the question mark; bitter is a British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquarelle is a painting in transparent watercolours, the sort of work exhibited by a watercolour society.

clue.text: In Scotland nimble old mare’s lapping loch

indicators.note: lapping means wrapping round, so the mare word encloses the loch abbreviation

blocks.note: yaud is a Scots word for an old mare
L is the map abbreviation for loch

explanation.surface: In the Highlands, a sprightly old horse drinks from a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside YAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Yauld is a Scots adjective for active, vigorous or agile, the same as nimble.

clue.text: Woodcutter’s tools for splitting bark from elms?

indicators.note: splitting breaks a word apart, so its letters are put back in another order
the bark is the outside of a tree, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
outside letters of elms

explanation.surface: A woodcutter's kit for stripping the bark off elm trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Tools for splitting looks like one phrase defining the answer, but for and splitting are wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A froe is a cleaving tool with a blade at right angles to its handle, used to split wood into shingles.
